The core mechanism of rat maze learning involves a transformation from innate sign-gestalt readiness (R) to refined mnemonized gestalt expectations (E), mediated by hierarchical chaining (H). These transitions form a dynamic system where each gestalt expectation acts as a node in a directed acyclic graph, enabling adaptive behavior. Transferability arises when readiness states (R) persist across mazes, indicating stable cognitive kernels. Fixation occurs when E stabilizes beyond optimal performance, halting further adaptation. The system exhibits non-linear dynamics: small changes in initial readiness can lead to divergent paths, while feedback loops between expectations and readiness create emergent behaviors. The breakdown regime manifests as loss of adaptability when H becomes rigid or E collapses into fixed patterns.
